properties.description: The Heaven None Missed (2015), directed by Kuntz Agus and starring Fedi Nuril, Laudya Cynthia Bella, and Raline Shah, is an Indonesian drama-romance that explores marriage, faith, and moral choice. An architect and family man marries a depressed woman to save her life, a decision that triggers deep emotional and marital conflict. The narrative emphasizes sacrifice, sincerity, and religious devotion as characters confront difficult choices, delivering a quietly intense, faith-inflected drama. The film combines intimate performances with contemplative pacing to probe themes of forgiveness and redemption.
properties.plot_summary: An architect who is already married and his family life are upended when he is compelled to marry a depressed woman in order to save her life. The new union strains his existing marriage, triggering emotional conflict, guilt, and moral dilemmas. The story traces the heroine's emotional journey from anger and resistance toward acceptance and sincere devotion, while examining sacrifice, faith, and personal choice. The film emphasizes quiet, religiously inflected moments and the difficult decisions that reshape relationships.

properties.description: Can You Ever Forgive Me? (2018), directed by Marielle Heller and starring Melissa McCarthy, Richard E. Grant and Dolly Wells, is a biographical crime drama with darkly comic touches. It follows a once-successful biographer who, facing professional decline and financial strain, forges letters from famous figures and sells them through a shady market, aided by a charismatic friend. The film is a slow-burning, character-driven study that explores themes of deception, authenticity, loneliness and moral consequence, anchored by nuanced performances and an intimate, period-accurate visual style.
properties.plot_summary: A once-successful biographer, displaced by changing tastes and financial hardship, turns her talent for mimicry into a scheme: forging letters from famous figures and selling them to collectors. Her partnership with a charming, self-destructive friend keeps the fraud afloat even as it deepens her ethical compromises and personal isolation. As attention mounts, their operation draws law-enforcement scrutiny and forces painful reckonings about loyalty, authenticity and consequence.
